## (3) New findings

### F1 — BLOCKER (a wrong result on an honest input; an undeclared behaviour shift) — CONFIRMED

* Where: `LiveIndex.relevant` (`packages/layout/src/infill/bentCutFabric.ts`, M0-b-03's) builds the subset a single
  mint reads from two chains — the entries on the record's `dup` chain by lineage, then the entries on its `~k` chain
  by address — and pushes both. When every entry at the fresh key's lineage is retired the dup loop stops there, the
  natural address is that lineage's, and a retired entry holding it is pushed a second time: the subset is `[E, E]`.
* Probe P4 (the committed Q70 fixture `twoDistricts`, run once, then again beside its own 239 entities marked
  `retired: true`; the input live set holds 241 entries, each id once):
  * the round's tree: `Error: tx 11/L1/callback/fn: mint: the live id way:f5aq4mcksb8zs is given twice` (thrown by
    `runS8`); the same input with the test seam `faults.wholeLiveMint` (every mint reads the whole list): ok;
  * with the guard removed (the pre-round mint): ok both ways, 239 minted, subset equal to whole list, every id the old
    one with `~1`, every lineage kept;
  * the control (the same entities as survivors, the committed test's shape): ok.
* Why it is a blocker and not a note: the input is lawful (each id once; `retired` marks "this batch re-derives it",
  and a retired entity at its own lineage and natural address is the faithful Regenerate the mint's header names); the
  result is a throw where the pre-round tree and the whole-list mint give the correct identities; the round caused it;
  C-0478 and the notes declare that no lawful input's output moves and that S8 hands the mint its own ids each once.
  It also breaks Q70's stated law for the fabric (the subset gives what the whole list gives).
* Reach: no M0 source builds a retired `LiveEntry` outside `model/src/identity` and `model/src/match` (`liveSetOf`, no
  caller outside its tests), and no test hands one to S8, so the gates stay green and the census does not rise. It is
  met by the first caller that re-derives a district beside its retired entities.
* Required change: see the failing line.

### The session's ruling on F1 (J741, 2026-11-10; it reached this lane before the verdict landed)

F1 STANDS as drafted (J741 (a)): the mint's refusal is right and stays as built — a list that names one id twice is not
a lawful set, and the mint cannot tell one entry listed twice from two holders — and the defect is the caller's. Of the
two routes the failing line offered, the session takes (a) and rejects (b)'s example (a mint that tolerates one entry
object listed twice). The remedy is the FIX ROUND's, under a cross-item write scope (J741 (c)): the body of
`LiveIndex.relevant` lists each `LiveEntry` once by object identity, in the order of first push, both loops walking as
they do; one new test file in `packages/layout/test/infill/fabric/` carries the pin (P4, the squatter variant, the
subset seen directly); a new choices row corrects C-0478's two statements and declares the shift as closed. The ruling
names two further shapes of the same doubling that this check's P4 did not execute (a retired entry at the final
lineage holding `natural~j`; a lineage-chain entry carrying a handed-on address on that chain): PLAUSIBLE from the
code read here (any entry on both chains is pushed twice), not probed by this seat — the fix round's pin and its
re-check own them. This check builds nothing of the remedy and edits no file of M0-b-03's.
